label: EU(7)-PIM: amantadine
title: Amantadine in an older person
statement: Amantadine | In lists: does not appear as PIM | Main reason: Risk of anticholinergic and CNS side effects including orthostatic hypotension, falls, sedation, weakness, confusion, amnesia | Dose adjustment/special considerations: Start with 100 mg/d in 2 divided daily doses. E | Alternatives: Levodopa; carbidopa-levodopa; benserazide levodopa; irreversible inhibitor of monoamine oxidase as rasagiline. E

plain_summary: Amantadine can cause confusion, hallucinations, falls and dizziness on standing in older people. For Parkinson's disease in people over 65, the Australian Symmetrel product information gives one whole 100 mg capsule daily. Reduced kidney function may require a longer interval between doses.
rule_for_models: Suspect a finding when a person aged 65 or older has at least one supply of amantadine (Group A). Any strength counts. If age is missing and amantadine is supplied, report only a possible finding and ask whether the person is 65 or older.
cannot_be_seen: Why amantadine was prescribed (Parkinson's disease, side effects of other medicines or flu prevention), kidney function, and whether the person has been confused or fallen.
ask_the_gp: Whether amantadine is still needed for this person, and whether the dose suits their kidney function.
